note: Both baseline and ablated runs produced a correct, specific diagnosis (src/parser.js:29, the precedence-handling bug in toRPN) even with filesystem.read:/workspace/src/** removed from the manifest. Root cause, checked directly: idhn.enforcement.filesystem.build_mount_plan has no loop over fs["read"] at all -- only "write" and "deny" patterns generate real mounts. The base workspace mount is read-only for the WHOLE tree regardless of what is in the read list; a read grant is audited by idhn.core.policy.PolicyEngine (which does check it) but is not itself OS-enforced, and nothing routes Codex's local file reads through that engine. So this ablation does not show "read access was unnecessary for diagnosis" -- it shows that removing a read grant currently has no mechanical enforcement effect at all, only explicit deny patterns and write grants have real teeth. A real architectural gap, not a compiler-recall finding; not fixed here per the freeze-and-observe instruction.
